title: Scheme components from a specified split reduced tensor algebra
statement: Let S and Z be affine schemes [def-weil-affine-spectrum], let g:Z\to S, and put A=\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S), B=\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z) with A-algebra structure induced by g. Let c\in A and let A-prime be a finite etale A[1/c]-algebra with compatible A-algebra structure, such that Spec(A-prime)\to Spec(A[1/c]) is surjective. Let D_j be A-prime-algebras indexed by Fin(r), with Spec(D_j)\to Spec(A-prime) universal homeomorphisms [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]. Suppose (B\otimes_A A-prime)/\sqrt{0} is isomorphic as A-prime-algebra to \prod_j D_j. There is a finite etale surjective cover p:T\to D(c), and r pairwise disjoint opens W_j covering Z\times_S T [def-pc-fibre-product], each with W_j\to T a universal homeomorphism. No nonzero condition on c or generic splitting existence is asserted.

source.place: Proof, finite-algebra calculation: after the reduced tensor algebra is split, take factor spectra and lift their open-and-closed components through reduction.

proof.text: Set A = Gamma(S,top), B = Gamma(Z,top), R = B tensor_A A-prime. Use the canonical affine spectrum identifications and the basicOpenIsoSpecAway isomorphism to identify U = D(c) with Spec(A[1/c]). Define T = Spec(A-prime) and p using this isomorphism. IsFinite.SpecMap_iff, the affine etale equivalence and hSurj give finiteness, etaleness and surjectivity of p. The tensor-product spectrum isomorphism identifies P = Z times_S T with Spec R, compatibly with P -> T.

Apply Spec to the supplied A-prime-algebra isomorphism R_red = product_j D_j. The finite affine coproduct-spectrum isomorphism makes the factor spectra pairwise disjoint open-and-closed subschemes covering Spec R_red, and identifies their maps to T with the supplied universal homeomorphisms. Pull the opens across the reduction homeomorphism to get W_j in Spec R. The zero-factor case is the empty spectrum of the zero ring, so the same covering statement holds.

Restrict the reduction closed immersion to each W_j. It is a surjective closed immersion, whose reduced domain is the specified factor spectrum. The morphism from W_j to T is integral because integrality is unchanged by a source thickening (take the identity thickening of T). Surjectivity follows from the surjectivity of its composite with reduction. After every base change the reduction immersion is surjective and its composite with W_j -> T is injective; lifting two points through the reduction shows that W_j -> T is universally injective. Thus it is a universal homeomorphism. Transport the opens and their maps through P = Spec R.

theorem finite_scheme_components_of_split_tensor_algebra
    (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine S] {Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine Z] (g : Z ⟶ S)
    (c : Γ(S, ⊤)) (A' : Type u) [CommRing A']
    [Algebra (Localization.Away c) A'] [Algebra Γ(S, ⊤) A']
    [IsScalarTower Γ(S, ⊤) (Localization.Away c) A']
    [Module.Finite (Localization.Away c) A']
    [Algebra.Etale (Localization.Away c) A']
    (hSurj : Surjective
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (Localization.Away c) A'))))
    (r : ℕ) (D : Fin r → Type u) [∀ j, CommRing (D j)] [∀ j, Algebra A' (D j)]
    (hD : ∀ j, IsUniversalHomeomorphism
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A' (D j)))))
    (he : letI := g.appTop.hom.toAlgebra
      letI := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra (R := Γ(S, ⊤)) (A := Γ(Z, ⊤)) (B := A')
      Nonempty (((Γ(Z, ⊤) ⊗[Γ(S, ⊤)] A') ⧸ _root_.nilradical (Γ(Z, ⊤) ⊗[Γ(S, ⊤)] A'))
        ≃ₐ[A'] (∀ j, D j))) :
    ∃ (T : Scheme.{u}) (p : T ⟶ (S.basicOpen c).toScheme),
      IsFinite p ∧ Etale p ∧ Surjective p ∧
      ∃ (W : Fin r → (pullback g (p ≫ (S.basicOpen c).ι)).Opens),
        (⨆ i, W i) = ⊤ ∧ Pairwise (fun i j ↦ Disjoint (W i) (W j)) ∧
        ∀ i, IsUniversalHomeomorphism
          ((W i).ι ≫ pullback.snd g (p ≫ (S.basicOpen c).ι))
